valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E. At the 12-month target date (Nov 2027) an investor prices FY2028 non-GAAP diluted EPS (Tesla non-GAAP excludes stock comp, digital-asset and SpaceX-stake marks). Starting point: Q3 2026 non-GAAP EPS $0.48 (net income $1,697M on 3,541M weighted diluted shares), GAAP $0.22, revenue about $28.0B flat y/y, gross margin 19.6%, operating income $718M (-56%) as opex rose 39%, FCF about $1.5B, cash and investments $45.4B. Management cut 2026 capex guidance to about $20B and signalled tens of billions by 2028. EPS paths and multiples are my own model assumptions, not company guidance; the multiple is a justified premium for autonomy/robotics optionality, so the result is highly sensitive to it.

bear.driver: Robotaxi/Optimus slip, auto volumes keep falling, capex and opex compress margins; FY2028 non-GAAP EPS stays below the 2025 level.

base.driver: Auto margin recovery on mix, services and energy growth, gradual Cybercab fleet ramp; opex growth slows; FY2028 EPS about 1.6x the Q3 annualized run rate ($1.92).

bull.driver: Unsupervised FSD and Cybercab scale in 2027, robotaxi and software revenue lift margins sharply.

valuation.implied_by_close: At base EPS $3.00 the $390.22 close implies 130x. The mean of the four non-GLJ named targets (about $424) implies 141x at base EPS, or EPS about $3.53 at 120x (18% above base EPS).
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $3.00 (0.8 pp of the close); $0.25 of FY2028 EPS moves it by $30 (7.7 pp).
valuation.watch_metric: Automotive gross margin ex-credits and operating margin, versus opex growth (39% y/y in Q3), plus Cybercab/robotaxi paid-mile volume and the 2027 capex level.
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 2026 results and shareholder update, expected late January 2027 (date not confirmed); Q4 deliveries report in early January 2027.

analyst_notes: Only named calls found: Piper Sandler raised to $475 from $450 after Q3 (Oct 22); Goldman kept $360 Neutral; Morgan Stanley Equal-weight $400 (Oct 16, pre-earnings, reported prior $415 conflicts in sources); GLJ Sell at $24.86 is an extreme outlier. All horizons are undocumented, so none enter the weighted target. The four non-GLJ targets (mean about $424) sit about 18% above base EPS or 141x versus 120x base multiple; the gap is a multiple/EPS difference whose analyst assumptions are unknown. JPMorgan reaffirmed Neutral $430 on 2026-11-16, after the reference close, and is excluded. Panel is small (4 analysts) versus about 40 in the Yahoo aggregate (mean $412.48).
